def factor_tail_downside_variance_ratio(df):
    """Lower downside variance relative to upside variance indicates tail-risk resilience."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    down_ret = np.minimum(ret, 0.0)
    up_ret = np.maximum(ret, 0.0)
    down_var = (down_ret ** 2).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    up_var = (up_ret ** 2).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    ratio = down_var / up_var.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ratio = ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + ratio)
    factor = factor.fillna(0.0)
    return pd.Series(factor, index=df_copy.index, name="factor_tail_downside_variance_ratio")
description: Measures asymmetric volatility: downside semi-variance relative to upside semi-variance over 60 days. Stocks with lower downside variance share exhibit tail-risk resilience; higher factor indicates lower tail-risk exposure. The mechanism focuses on volatility asymmetry rather than generic moving-average or stacked-indicator patterns.
